memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Say to the assembly, 'Move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan and Abiram.'" Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him. He warned the assembly, "Move back from the tents of these wicked men! Do not touch anything belonging to them, or you will be swept away because of all their sins." So they moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan and Abiram. — Num 16:23-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's mercy in answer to Moses' prayer takes a practical form: He gives the people a way to escape the coming judgment. "Move away from the tents." Those who were willing to separate themselves from the rebels would be spared. Mercy provided an exit, but the people had to take it.

There is wisdom here about the company we keep and the influences we allow near us. Sin is not always contained; it can spread and sweep others into its consequences. God graciously warned the people to distance themselves from the rebellion before it dragged them down with it. Sometimes love for God means putting real distance between ourselves and what opposes Him.

Notice that the people had to act on the warning. It was not enough to hear it; they had to get up and move. God's provision of an escape required their response. The same is true for us. God warns us, in His word, of the paths that lead to ruin and calls us to turn away from them. But we must actually heed the warning and step back.

This is not about looking down on others as if we are better; it is about not entangling ourselves in what we know is against God. Scripture calls us to come out and be separate, not in pride but in faithfulness. And the ultimate rescue is found in Christ, who calls us out of the kingdom of darkness into His kingdom of light. The great separation He accomplished was to move us from death to life. In gratitude, we heed His call to walk away from sin and toward Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there influences in your life you need to put distance from?
2. Why is it not enough merely to hear God's warnings without acting on them?
3. How does Christ's rescue from darkness shape the way you live?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for warning me away from paths that lead to ruin. Give me the wisdom and courage to put distance between myself and what opposes You. Thank You that in Christ You have called me out of darkness into Your light. Amen.
